title: Work timestamps
summary: Each finished turn's fold row in the thread timeline names when the work ended, next to how long it took: "Worked for 3m 30s · 9:42 PM EST", "You stopped after 12s · 9:42 PM EST", and "Continued for …" on the rows below a steer. The time is the instant the duration is measured to, in the system's locale (12- or 24-hour) and time zone, without seconds, with the month and day added when the turn ended before today; the label gains its date at local midnight. Rows still working, and rows without a duration, show no time. The label strings take the time as a placeholder, translated in every web catalog.

checks.name: fold label logic
checks.run: . "$T3_PATCHER_ENV" && cd apps/web && pnpm exec vp test run --project unit src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.logic.test.ts

checks.name: fold row and midnight rollover
checks.run: . "$T3_PATCHER_ENV" && export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="${PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH:-$BE/ms-playwright}" && cd apps/web && pnpm exec playwright install chromium && pnpm exec vp test run --project browser src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.browser.test.tsx

journeys.name: work_timestamps
journeys.proves: A fixture ACP agent runs a turn with a finished tool call between two messages in the built app; the thread's fold row reads "Worked for <duration> · <time>", where the time is a minute the turn ended in, formatted in the Mac's own locale and time zone (with the date only when that minute isn't today), without seconds.
